fr.obj.greetings.basic.title: Everyday greetings & politeness
fr.obj.greetings.basic.canDo: I can recognise and write the everyday French greetings and politeness formulas — bonjour, bonsoir, salut, au revoir, merci, s'il vous plaît — and pick the right one for the situation.

fr.obj.vocab.everyday_basics.title: Core everyday nouns
fr.obj.vocab.everyday_basics.canDo: I can understand and name the course's core everyday words — people, food and drink, animals, and other common everyday things — when I read them.

fr.obj.vocab.places_travel.title: Places & travel words
fr.obj.vocab.places_travel.canDo: I can understand the French words for common places and travel needs — la ville, la gare, l'hôtel, le billet — when I read them.

fr.obj.vocab.time_calendar.title: Time & calendar words
fr.obj.vocab.time_calendar.canDo: I can use the French words for counting time — le jour, l'heure, la minute, la semaine, le mois, l'année.

fr.obj.reading.familiar_words.title: Reading familiar words & short phrases
fr.obj.reading.familiar_words.canDo: I can recognise familiar French words and very short learned phrases when I see them written, and match them to their meaning.

fr.obj.writing.familiar_words.title: Writing familiar words & forms
fr.obj.writing.familiar_words.canDo: I can type familiar French words and learned forms with the right spelling, including accents — mangé, être, vingt et un.

fr.obj.gender.articles_basic.title: Articles with familiar nouns
fr.obj.gender.articles_basic.canDo: I can choose the right article — le or la, un or une — for the familiar nouns I have learned.

fr.obj.gender.ending_patterns.title: Gender from word endings
fr.obj.gender.ending_patterns.canDo: I can use reliable French endings — -tion, -ance, -ité, -ment, -age, -eau — to predict whether a new noun takes le or la.

fr.obj.verbs.etre_avoir_present.title: Être & avoir in the present
fr.obj.verbs.etre_avoir_present.canDo: I can use the present-tense forms of être and avoir with every subject — je suis, tu as, nous sommes, ils ont.

fr.obj.verbs.er_present.title: Regular -er verbs in the present
fr.obj.verbs.er_present.canDo: I can conjugate regular -er verbs like parler, aimer and habiter in the present tense for every subject.

fr.obj.verbs.aller_faire_present.title: Aller & faire in the present
fr.obj.verbs.aller_faire_present.canDo: I can use the present-tense forms of aller and faire — je vais, elle va, nous faisons, ils font.

fr.obj.verbs.futur_proche.title: Near future with aller
fr.obj.verbs.futur_proche.canDo: I can talk about plans by putting aller in front of any verb — Je vais manger, Nous allons parler.

fr.obj.verbs.passe_compose_avoir.title: Past tense with avoir
fr.obj.verbs.passe_compose_avoir.canDo: I can build the everyday past tense with avoir plus a participle — J'ai mangé, Tu as parlé — for the verbs I know.

fr.obj.numbers.0_100.title: Numbers 0-100
fr.obj.numbers.0_100.canDo: I can understand and write every French number from zéro to cent, including the et-un pattern, soixante-dix and quatre-vingts.

fr.obj.connected.elision.title: Elision in writing
fr.obj.connected.elision.canDo: I can apply mandatory French elision in writing — l'eau, j'ai, ce n'est pas — and never write je ai or le homme.

fr.obj.connected.liaison_h.title: Liaison & the two h's
fr.obj.connected.liaison_h.canDo: I can recognise where French links words together — les amis, nous avons — where it never does, and why l'histoire but le héros.

fr.obj.strategy.cognate_transfer.title: Cognate bridges & false friends
fr.obj.strategy.cognate_transfer.canDo: I can use the -tion and -té bridges to understand new French words from English — and I know the classic traps like librairie and journée.
